subject: Aurora: sudden latency + 5xx spike in AZ3 — exec bridge requested
messages:
From: Alex Torres <atorres@auroratech.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@auroratech.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2029 09:21:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: major latency and 502 spike from AZ3 (Aurora)

Dylan —

We started seeing a sharp latency increase and a flooding of 502s out of AZ3 around 08:55 PT. Our service level drops below 60% P95 and user sessions are failing. This is hitting our payment flow and homepage.

Attached are a short trace bundle and a handful of error samples. Can you confirm whether this is a regional issue on your side or if there is something in our config? We need an ETA; this is customer-impacting and senior leadership is already on it.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Torres
SRE Lead, AuroraTech

Attachments: aurora_az3_trace_20291115.zip (trace bundle), aurora_error_samples.txt (sample logs)
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@auroratech.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <psingh@auroratech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2029 09:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: major latency and 502 spike from AZ3 (Aurora)

Alex —

Thanks for the traces, digging in now. Initial quick check: we’re seeing elevated queue depth and token scheduling delays on AZ3 for the redwood-dedicated pool backing your routes. Error rate jump (502) aligns with overloaded worker restarts around 08:54.

Immediate actions I’m taking:
- Opening an incident bridge and triage channel.
- Launching a temporary cross-region steer to route new requests to us-west2 for customers tagged aurora-prod.
- Asking infra to provision burst capacity (2x) to drain queues in AZ3.

I’ll update in 10 minutes with metrics and whether the steer is holding.

—Dylan
Dylan Brooks
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2029 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Urgent: major latency and 502 spike from AZ3 (Aurora)

Team —

Forwarding Aurora thread. TL;DR: P95 latency > 2.3s and 5xx rate ~7% starting 08:55 PT. Dylan has started a cross-region steer to us-west2 but we need exec signoff for two items:

1) Temporary priority capacity on Western pool (will incur overage and require approval).
2) A customer-facing note and a goodwill credit (Aurora is on enterprise plan and this affects billing cycle).

Hannah — can you join the bridge and advise on SLA/credit authority? Rishi — please evaluate whether an automated fallback to the smaller quantized variant (latency-optimized) would be safe as a second fallback.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2029 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: major latency and 502 spike from AZ3 (Aurora)

Thanks all — joining the bridge now.

Marissa: approve temporary priority capacity up to 4 hours to stabilize user-facing traffic. Please proceed with the steer Dylan initiated — prioritize routing for payment endpoints.

Alex: we will proactively route new traffic to us-west2 for the next 90 minutes while we investigate AZ3 health. We’ll also prepare a short customer notification; Priya, can you confirm which endpoints are affected and we’ll tailor the message.

I’ll circulate a one-line exec note after we confirm the initial mitigation holds.

- Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
VP, Customer Ops, Redwood Inference
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Alex Torres <atorres@auroratech.com>
Date: Fri, 15 Nov 2029 10:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Urgent: major latency and 502 spike from AZ3 (Aurora)

Update from infra/serving team:
- Root cause hypothesis: autoscaler mis-signal combined with a kernel-level memory pressure on a subset of AZ3 hosts led to slow KV cache hot-paths and worker restarts.
- Mitigation applied: drained 60% of traffic off AZ3, hot-patched the scheduler to reduce batch-size under pressure, and restarted problematic instances.
- Observed effect: 5xx rate reduced to ~0.7% and P95 improved to 850ms in us-west2; AZ3 still fluctuates between 1.6s–2.1s for P95.

Safe fallback options to recommend:
- Continue cross-region steer (recommended) and enable quantized latency-optimized variant for payment endpoints for 1 hour as a conservative fallback.
- If AZ3 fails to stabilize within 3 hours, execute a full evacuation and reroute to us-west2 permanently until root cause is fixed.

I’ve created Jira INF-7123 for postmortem action items.
Rishi
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Torres <atorres@auroratech.com>, Priya Singh <psingh@auroratech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 16 Nov 2029 02:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Post-mitigation update: AZ3 routed + next steps

Alex/Priya —

Quick post-mortem update from the bridge:
- What we did: temporary cross-region steer to us-west2, priority capacity for Aurora for 3 hours, batch-scheduler patch, and targeted restarts.
- Current status: customer-facing latency is back within SLOs for routed traffic; AZ3 continues to show intermittent pressure but no new 502 surge in last 90 minutes.
- Next steps:
  - Rishi’s team will run a deeper memory/kernel trace and escalate to infra kernel team if recurrence is seen (Jira INF-7123).
  - We’ll keep the steer in place for 4 hours total and then move to a gradual traffic reintroduction to AZ3 with canary checks.
  - Marissa to follow up on a goodwill credit + customer note draft.

Thanks for the quick coordination. We’ll share a concise incident summary and timeline when the postmortem is ready.

Best,
Dylan
Customer Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
